Elder Collins: Julio, let me introduce you to Elder Ramos and Elder Fifita.
Julio greets them with affection, but his face shows a lot of sadness.
Julio: I'm only going to keep going to church if you stay here.
Elder Collins: I'd stay if I could, but my transfer is already decided.
Elder Collins: Your conversion is to Christ, not to a missionary.
Julio admits that he feels fear about arriving at the chapel alone and not knowing anyone.
Elder Collins: What would help you feel comfortable with them?
Julio: It would help me to have a family home evening with them here at my house.
Elder Collins: The elders would come every week, as long as you text them.
Elder Collins: Brother Treviño, could you go to church with him on Sunday?
Brother Treviño offers his support: I would pick you up at 9, as long as you let me know if you change plans.
Elder Collins sets a clear condition: Don't stop coming, unless you're sick.
Elder Fifita: Attendance at sacrament meeting would give you strength for the whole week.
Elder Collins: You'll be fine as long as you pray and read every day.
Julio takes a deep breath and promises consistency in his prayers so he can stay faithful to the Lord.
In the end, everyone hugs, and the goodbye ends with a prayer and a lot of affection.

example.target: Elder Collins no se queda en San Bernardino.
example.native: Elder Collins doesn't stay in San Bernardino.

example.native: The elders come every week.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form (vengo) and stem change e to ie (vienes), except nosotros. Conditional: vendrían.

example.target: El hermano Treviño ayuda a Julio los domingos.
example.native: Brother Treviño helps Julio on Sundays.

passage.title: Un sábado de bautismo difícil
target: El sábado, Elder Hayes, como entrenador, empieza el entrenamiento de Elder Noé Batista en la capilla de la rama de Ensenada.
Elder Hayes: Elder Batista, ayúdame con la lista; no abras la llave todavía.
A las 2, el hermano Castro, uno de los testigos del bautismo de Daniela Soto, llama porque está enfermo y no puede venir.
Elder Hayes necesita un testigo suplente y busca al hermano Rubio, que está acomodando sillas en el salón cultural.
Elder Hayes: Hermano Rubio, ¿podría ser testigo si el presidente de rama lo aprueba?
El presidente Lara lo aprueba, pero luego hay una discusión entre Lupita Reyes y Saúl Ibarra sobre el programa.
La hermana Reyes quiere dirigir el himno de apertura, pero el hermano Ibarra dice que ella le prometió que él lo dirigiría.
Elder Hayes: Hermana Reyes, hermano Ibarra, quiero escuchar a los dos primero.
Después de escucharlos, Elder Hayes propone una solución: ella dirige el himno de apertura y él da el discurso sobre el bautismo.
Elder Hayes: ¿Les parecería bien si cada uno tiene una parte del programa?
Durante el discurso, una invitada, la señora Marta Gil, se desmaya; segundos después está consciente, pero muy pálida.
Elder Hayes le dice al hermano Rubio: Hermano, llame al 911 ahora; yo me quedo con ella.
El operador del servicio de emergencias pide que la dejen acostada y que abran una puerta para que entre aire fresco.
Cuando Elder Batista trae agua, Elder Hayes le dice: Elder, no le des nada hasta que nos diga el operador.
Llegan los paramédicos, Daniela se bautiza sin problemas y esa noche Elder Hayes dicta el resumen del día.
Elder Hayes dicta: Una invitada se desmayó; sin embargo, los paramédicos la atendieron enseguida.
Elder Hayes agrega: Además, el hermano Rubio sirvió de testigo suplente; por lo tanto, sugeriría que siempre tuviéramos uno listo.
Al final, Elder Hayes le dice a Elder Batista: Hiciste muy bien hoy, Elder; mañana repasamos lo que aprendimos.
native: On Saturday, Elder Hayes, as trainer, begins Elder Noé Batista's training in the chapel of the Ensenada branch.
Elder Hayes: Elder Batista, help me with the checklist; don't turn on the water yet.
At 2, Brother Castro, one of the witnesses for Daniela Soto's baptism, calls because he is sick and can't come.
Elder Hayes needs a substitute witness and looks for Brother Rubio, who is setting up chairs in the cultural hall.
Elder Hayes: Brother Rubio, could you be a witness if the branch president approves?
President Lara approves, but then there is an argument between Lupita Reyes and Saúl Ibarra about the program.
Sister Reyes wants to lead the opening hymn, but Brother Ibarra says she promised him that he would lead it.
Elder Hayes: Sister Reyes, Brother Ibarra, I want to hear from both of you first.
After listening to them, Elder Hayes proposes a solution: she leads the opening hymn and he gives the talk about baptism.
Elder Hayes: Would it be all right if each of you has a part of the program?
During the talk, a guest, Mrs. Marta Gil, faints; a few seconds later she is conscious, but very pale.
Elder Hayes tells Brother Rubio: Brother, call 911 now; I'll stay with her.
The emergency services dispatcher asks them to keep her lying down and to open a door to let fresh air in.
When Elder Batista brings water, Elder Hayes tells him: Elder, don't give her anything until the dispatcher tells us.
The paramedics arrive, Daniela is baptized without problems, and that night Elder Hayes dictates the summary of the day.
Elder Hayes dictates: A guest fainted; however, the paramedics took care of her right away.
Elder Hayes adds: In addition, Brother Rubio served as substitute witness; therefore, I would suggest we always have one ready.
At the end, Elder Hayes tells Elder Batista: You did really well today, Elder; tomorrow we'll go over what we learned.

example.target: Elder Batista, ayúdame con la lista.
example.native: Elder Batista, help me with the checklist.

verbs.note: Informal tú command ayuda; attach the pronoun: ayúdame.

example.target: Hermano, llame al 911 ahora.
example.native: Brother, call 911 now.

verbs.note: Formal usted command: llame. Use llamar a before a number or a person.

example.target: Elder Hayes escucha a los dos primero.
example.native: Elder Hayes listens to both of them first.

verbs.note: No preposition needed for 'to listen to'; use the personal a before people.

example.target: Yo me quedo con ella.
example.native: I'll stay with her.

verbs.note: Reflexive; quedarse con alguien means to stay with someone.

example.target: La hermana Reyes dirige el himno de apertura.
example.native: Sister Reyes leads the opening hymn.

verbs.note: Spelling change g to j in the yo form only: dirijo.
